OpenWrt Presence provides fast, local, event-driven Wi-Fi presence tracking for
Home Assistant. This is the first public release.

## Highlights

- Creates native Home Assistant device trackers from authenticated OpenWrt
  Presence Agent observations.
- Applies valid association changes immediately over one persistent WebSocket
  connection without an integration polling interval.
- Recovers stream integrity from authoritative snapshots.
- Represents observer or stream failure as `unavailable` instead of fabricating
  an away event.
- Keeps evidence from multiple observers source-specific.
- Creates new trackers disabled by default to avoid unnecessary recorder load.
- Supports UI configuration, reauthentication, reconfiguration, options, and
  clean unload.

## Requirements

- Home Assistant 2026.7 or newer.
- OpenWrt Presence Agent API v1.
- Network reachability from Home Assistant to the observer.

The complete router-to-Home Assistant path has been live-tested only with a
GL.iNet Flint 3 (`GL-BE9300`) running GL.iNet firmware 4.9.0. Other routers
remain community-test candidates even when a matching agent package builds.

## Installation

Add
`https://github.com/theoabw/ha-openwrt-presence`
to HACS as a custom integration repository, download this release, restart Home
Assistant, and add **OpenWrt Presence** under **Settings → Devices & services**.

See the
[README](https://github.com/theoabw/ha-openwrt-presence/blob/v0.1.0/README.md)
for agent setup, tracker enablement, stable phone MAC guidance, state semantics,
security considerations, and troubleshooting.

The release archive is covered by `SHA256SUMS` and a GitHub build-provenance
attestation.
